Plot a conditional chemical shift histogram

Source: R/histogram.R
conditional_cs_hist.Rd

Shows the CS distribution of `atom` in `residue` before and after filtering by known chemical shifts of other atoms in the same residue. Mirrors `pybmrb.Histogram.conditional_hist()`.

conditional_cs_hist(
  residue,
  atom,
  filtering_rules,
  ph_min = NULL,
  ph_max = NULL,
  t_min = NULL,
  t_max = NULL,
  h_tolerance = 0.1,
  c_tolerance = 2,
  n_tolerance = 2,
  standard_amino_acids = TRUE,
  histnorm = NULL,
  plot_type = "histogram",
  output_format = "html",
  output_file = NULL,
  output_image_width = 800,
  output_image_height = 600,
  show_visualization = TRUE
)

Arguments

residue

Residue name.

atom

Atom whose distribution to plot.

filtering_rules

Named list of atom = value pairs used to filter, e.g. `list(CA = 64.5, H = 7.8)`.

ph_min, ph_max, t_min, t_max

Condition filters.

h_tolerance

Tolerance (ppm) for H filters. Default 0.1.

c_tolerance

Tolerance (ppm) for C filters. Default 2.0.

n_tolerance

Tolerance (ppm) for N filters. Default 2.0.

standard_amino_acids

Restrict to standard amino acids. Default TRUE.

histnorm

Normalisation (see [cs_hist()]).

plot_type

"histogram" (default), "box", or "violin".

output_format, output_file, output_image_width, output_image_height, show_visualization

See [cs_hist()].

Value

Invisibly, a list with `all_values`, `filtered_values`, `labels`.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  conditional_cs_hist("SER", "N",
    filtering_rules = list(CA = 55.5, HA = 4.3))
} # }
